answer_parts.text: The Oracle errors indicate that the database connection has become invalid after being idle: Oracle can close it because of its maximum idle-time setting, while WebSphere’s connection pool still considers it active. This results in a StaleConnectionException when the connection is reused.
Configure the WebSphere data-source connection pool with Minimum connections set to 0. This prevents idle connections from being retained solely to satisfy the minimum-pool requirement.
Set Unused timeout and Reap timeout so their sum does not exceed the network or database idle-connection timeout.
In the WebSphere administrative console, go to Resources → JDBC → Data sources, edit the connection-pool settings for the affected data source, and restart the servers after applying the changes.

answer_parts.text: AMQ9640 with reason code 2399 occurs because the client-side SSLPEERNAME was erroneously populated from the distinguished name (DN) of the certificate during the JMS Session connection. That unintended peer-name comparison then failed; the SSL connection itself had already been established.
The reported defect affects WebSphere MQ Classes for JMS V7.0.1 SSL connections and is specifically documented with the same JmqiException and MQRC_SSL_PEER_NAME_ERROR pattern.
The IBM fix changed the JMS classes so they no longer set SSLPEERNAME from the certificate DN during the JMS Session connection. For MQ 7.0, the fix was targeted for maintenance level 7.0.1.13.

A separate possible cause is malformed DN parsing: slashes in certificate DN fields such as CN, O, OU, or L can cause SSLPEER verification and the SSL handshake to fail because MQ uses slash characters as DN delimiters. The documented workaround is to generate certificates whose DN values contain no slashes.

resolved_support.text: Web Services HTTP HTTPS MustGather; MustGathers; Must Gather; Collect Troubleshooting Data; MustGatherDocument; Collecting; Trouble; Shooting TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING) PROBLEM(ABSTRACT) You are experiencing Web Services (HTTP, HTTPS) problems with WebSphere Message Broker (WMB) or IBM Integration Bus (IIB) on UNIXes and Linux. This mustgather document explains how to troubleshoot this problem by yourself, how to generate diagnostic data when the problem is happening, how to collect the available data from your system, and how to share that data with IBM support. ENVIRONMENT These instructions are for WebSphere Message Broker or IBM Integration Bus on AIX, HP-UX, Linux, and Solaris systems. Return to the WebSphere Message Broker MustGather index [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21209857] for other systems. RESOLVING THE PROBLEM STEP 1: SELF-GUIDED TROUBLESHOOTING 1. Consider Using the Test Client in trace and debug mode [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSMKHH_9.0.0/com.ibm.etools.mft.doc/af52260_.htm]. 2. 3. A user level trace [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=849&uid=swg21177321#1] is intended to assist users with understanding how their ESQL is processed. It will also show a high level view of the message flow behavior. 4. 5. Check for known issues: Dynamic guide to help troubleshooting Message Broker [https://www.ibm.com/developerworks/community/blogs/c7e1448b-9651-456c-9924-f78bec90d2c2/entry/try_a_dynamic_guide_to_help_with_troubleshooting_message_broker?lang=en] IIB and Web services [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSMKHH_9.0.0/com.ibm.etools.mft.doc/ac55700_.htm] Implementing WebService security in WMB [http://www.ibm.com/developerworks/websphere/library/techarticles/1008_fan/1008_fan.html] Run the WebServices samples [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSMKHH_9.0.0/com.ibm.etools.mft.doc/ax20230_.htm?cp=SSMKHH_9.0.0%2F1-2-4] [http://www.ibm.com/software/htp/cics/tserver/support/]WebSphere Message Broker support site [http://www.ibm.com/support/entry/portal/Overview/Software/WebSphere/WebSphere_Message_Broker] STEP 2: COLLECT DATA 1. mqsidc See: mqsidc usage instructions [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSMKHH_9.0.0/com.ibm.etools.mft.doc/bu46012_.htm] * This command line tool is only available for WMB 7.0.0.5+, WMB 8.0.0.1+, and IIB 9.0. * When running the tool, select the option for 'Broker Collector', when prompted. 2. 3. Project Interchange files for the problematic flow/set/ESQL/model * You can export your Message Flow and Message Set project(s) into an archive file for easy transmission to IBM Support. See: Exporting files from the Workbench [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSMKHH_9.0.0/com.ibm.etools.mft.doc/ax20230_.htm?cp=SSMKHH_9.0.0%2F1-2-4] 4. 5. Traces If the problem occurs during a runtime test or with the Toolkit test facility, WMB execution group traces [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=849&uid=swg21177321] can be used to gain a better understanding of the problem. * A service level trace [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=849&uid=swg21177321#2] is intended to be provided to IBM Support to assist in the diagnosis of your issue. * [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=849&uid=swg21177049]SSL trace [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21300238] for HTTPS problems only * [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=849&uid=swg21177049]SOAP debug trace [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21660124] when using SOAP nodes with http (not https) 6. 7. General Broker information If the mqsidc tool was not run, then capture this information manually * Record the IBM Integration Bus or WebSphere Message Broker version, release, and maintenance level. This can be captured using the command 'mqsiservice -v'.. * Record the operating system version, release, and maintenance level. * Record the version, release, and maintenance level of any related products and components for the problematic application. * Collect the local error log. On UNIX and Linux systems, the local error log is the syslog. The location of your syslog is configured in the syslog daemon. See: Configuring the syslog daemon [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSMKHH_9.0.0/com.ibm.etools.mft.doc/an04230_.htm] * Collect the Standard Output/Error logs. WMB writes information to both STDOUT and STDERR. These files are located under the Message Broker workpath. See: Standard System Logs

resolved_support.text: SECURITY BULLETIN SUMMARY Vulnerabilities in .NET Core, ASP.NET Core Could Allow Elevation of Privilege. Vulnerabilities in Node.js and the c-ares library were disclosed on July 11 2017 by the Node.js Foundation. IBM SDK for Node.js has addressed the applicable CVEs. VULNERABILITY DETAILS CVEID: CVE-2017-0256 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2017-0256] DESCRIPTION: Microsoft ASP.NET Core could allow a remote attacker to conduct spoofing attacks, caused by improper validation of user supplied input. CVSS Base Score: 6.5 CVSS Temporal Score: See https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/125327 [https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/125327] for the current score CVSS Environmental Score*: Undefined CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N) CVEID: CVE-2017-0249 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2017-0249] DESCRIPTION: Microsoft ASP.NET Core could allow a remote attacker to gain elevated privileges on the system, caused by improper validation of user supplied input. CVSS Base Score: 8.4 CVSS Temporal Score: See https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/125299 [https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/125299] for the current score CVSS Environmental Score*: Undefined CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.0/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H) CVEID: CVE-2017-0247 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2017-0247] DESCRIPTION: Microsoft ASP.NET Core is vulnerable to a denial of service, caused by improper validation of web requests in the TextEncoder.EncodeCore function. By inserting specially-crafted content into any system using the function to encode content, a remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability to prevent any page delivering the content from loading. CVSS Base Score: 3.6 CVSS Temporal Score: See https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/125297 [https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/125297] for the current score CVSS Environmental Score*: Undefined CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.0/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:N/I:N/A:L) CVEID: CVE-2017-1000381 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2017-1000381] DESCRIPTION: c-ares could allow a remote attacker to obtain sensitive information, caused by an out-of-bounds read in the ares_parse_naptr_reply() function when parsing NAPTR responses. By sending specially crafted DNS response packet, an attacker could exploit this vulnerability to read memory outside of the given input buffer and cause a denial of service. CVSS Base Score: 6.5 CVSS Temporal Score: See https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/128625 [https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/128625] for the current score CVSS Environmental Score*: Undefined CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:L) CVEID: CVE-2017-11499 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2017-11499] DESCRIPTION: Node.js is vulnerable to a denial of service, caused by a flaw related to constant HashTable seeds. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability to flood the hash and cause a denial of service. CVSS Base Score: 7.5 CVSS Temporal Score: See https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/129465 [https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/129465] for the current score CVSS Environmental Score*: Undefined CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H) AFFECTED PRODUCTS AND VERSIONS These vulnerabilities affect ASP.NET Core in IBM Bluemix v1.0.20 and earlier releases. answer_parts.text: The JOBTASK long description is stored in the LONGDESCRIPTION table, not directly as a nested JOBTASK description field. Query it by matching `LDOWNERTABLE = 'JOBTASK'`, `LDOWNERCOL = 'DESCRIPTION'`, and `LDKEY` to the relevant JOBTASK IDs.
For example, first obtain the job plan ID: `SELECT JOBPLANID FROM JOBPLAN WHERE JPNUM='IT-ISSUE'`. The documented example returns `JOBPLANID = 51`.

Then use that ID in the long-description query: `SELECT LDTEXT FROM LONGDESCRIPTION WHERE LDOWNERTABLE='JOBTASK' AND LDOWNERCOL='DESCRIPTION' AND LDKEY IN (SELECT JOBTASK.JOBTASKID FROM JOBTASK WHERE JOBTASK.JOBPLANID = 51)`
Do not use an outer join between JOBTASK and LONGDESCRIPTION when querying the long-description text.

answer_parts.text: The pattern is showing MQ 8.0.0.2 because the deployed environment is using an affected IBM MQ PureApplication System pattern type (1.0.0.2 or earlier) with PureApplication System 2.1.2.0, 2.2.0.0, or later. An interface change causes installation of the latest maintenance level in the pattern to fail silently: deployment appears successful, but MQ 8.0.0.2 is installed and the subsequent fix-pack update is not applied.

On PureApplication System 2.1.2.0, 2.2.0.0, and later, the affected pattern types can install only MQ 8.0.0.2; later versions such as 8.0.0.4 cannot be installed, and maintenance cannot be applied to running pattern instances.

The documented resolution is to obtain and install the updated maintenance.py lifecycle script, which enables installation or migration to the latest MQ maintenance level contained in the pattern type. The update and installation steps are available from IBM Fix Central; APAR IT15252 was raised for this issue.

suppressed_parts.text: The pattern is showing MQ 8.0.0.2 because the deployed environment is using an affected IBM MQ PureApplication System pattern type (1.0.0.2 or earlier) with PureApplication System 2.1.2.0, 2.2.0.0, or later. An interface change causes installation of the latest maintenance level in the pattern to fail silently: deployment appears successful, but MQ 8.0.0.2 is installed and the subsequent fix-pack update is not applied.

valid_parts.text: On PureApplication System 2.1.2.0, 2.2.0.0, and later, the affected pattern types can install only MQ 8.0.0.2; later versions such as 8.0.0.4 cannot be installed, and maintenance cannot be applied to running pattern instances.

The documented resolution is to obtain and install the updated maintenance.py lifecycle script, which enables installation or migration to the latest MQ maintenance level contained in the pattern type. The update and installation steps are available from IBM Fix Central; APAR IT15252 was raised for this issue.

This affects IBM MQ PureApplication System pattern types 1.0.0.2 and earlier; on PureApplication System 2.1.2.0, 2.2.0.0, and later, those pattern types can install only MQ 8.0.0.2 and cannot install later versions such as 8.0.0.4 or apply maintenance to running pattern instances.

IBM provided a new maintenance.py lifecycle script to enable installation and migration to the latest MQ maintenance level contained in the pattern type; the update and installation steps are available from IBM Fix Central. answer_parts.text: The information is in the IBM API Connect Security Bulletin, particularly its “Vulnerability Details” section for CVE-2017-14919. The vulnerability is a Node.js zlib uncaught-exception flaw that can let a remote attacker crash the application by using an invalid windowBits value of 8. Its CVSS base score is 7.5.
The bulletin lists IBM API Connect versions 5.0.0.0–5.0.6.4, 5.0.7.0–5.0.7.2, and 5.0.8.0–5.0.8.1 as affected.
For remediation, IBM API Connect 5.0.0.0–5.0.6.4 is addressed in version 5.0.6.5 under APAR LI79994.

resolved_support.text:
SUMMARY
 IBM API Connect has addressed the following vulnerability.

Node.js is vulnerable to a denial of service, caused by an uncaught exception flaw in the zlib module. By making 8 an invalid value for the windowBits parameter, a remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability to cause the application to crash.

VULNERABILITY DETAILS
CVEID:CVE-2017-14919 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2017-14919]
DESCRIPTION:Node.js is vulnerable to a denial of service, caused by an uncaught exception flaw in the zlib module. By making 8 an invalid value for the windowBits parameter, a remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability to cause the application to crash.
CVSS Base Score: 7.5
CVSS Temporal Score: Seehttps://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/134286 [https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/134286]for the current score
CVSS Environmental Score*: Undefined
CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H)

answer_parts.text: Use the database-specific current-date expression rather than `TODAY()`: on DB2 use `CURRENT DATE`, on Oracle use `sysdate`, and on Microsoft SQL Server use `getdate()`.

For a date/time field such as `reportdate`, a same-day range should use the start of today through the start of tomorrow—for example, on DB2: `reportdate >= CURRENT DATE AND reportdate < (CURRENT DATE + 1 DAY)`; on Oracle: `reportdate >= TRUNC(sysdate) AND reportdate < TRUNC(sysdate) + 1`; on SQL Server: `reportdate >= CAST(getdate() AS date) AND reportdate < DATEADD(day, 1, CAST(getdate() AS date))`.

answer_parts.text: The documented issue is not a general incompatibility between the BPM internal Document Store and IBM DB2 pureScale. During FileNet Content Manager object-store add-on creation, having multiple DB2 pureScale members active can cause excessive SQL locking, lock timeouts, transaction rollbacks, and add-on installation failure.

To resolve it, leave only one DB2 pureScale member active while installing the FileNet CM add-on/internal document store. After the installation completes successfully, bring the other members back online.

To diagnose this condition, check the P8 error log and the DB2 diagnostic log for each active member. DB2 may report SQLP_LTIMEOUT with reason code 68, while the P8 log may report a deadlock and SQLCODE=-911; SQLERRMC=68 indicates that the underlying cause is a SQL lock timeout.

resolved_support.text:
DIAGNOSING THE PROBLEM
MON_GET_TABLESPACE table function and RECLAIMABLE_SPACE_ENABLED monitor element can be used to identify whether the tablespace is enabled for reclaimable storage or not. Example: 
db2 "SELECT varchar(tbsp_name, 30) as tbsp_name, tbsp_type, RECLAIMABLE_SPACE_ENABLED FROM TABLE(MON_GET_TABLESPACE('',-2))"
If the RECLAIMABLE_SPACE_ENABLED monitor element returns a value of 1, then the tablespace is enabled for reclaimable storage. Otherwise, it returns a value of 0.

 Can I download the software without active Subscription and Maintenance?

answer_parts.text: After upgrading to v7.5.2 or later, SSH may reject connections because legacy key-exchange algorithms—including diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha1 and diffie-hellman-group1-sha1—and MD5-based MAC algorithms are disabled by default. A peer that supports only those older algorithms has no mutually supported algorithm, so the connection fails even though the same configuration worked on v7.2.
Typical errors are “No matching cipher found,” “No matching MAC algorithm found,” or “No matching kex algorithm found.”

For a permanent fix, upgrade the SSH client or server so it supports the safer algorithms in the new default lists. As a temporary workaround, enable the required legacy algorithms; on DataPower, the SSH server profile supports enable-legacy-kex in 7.5.2.0, while the SSH client profile supports it in 7.5.2.7.

answer_parts.text: SSH connections fail after the upgrade because the newer SSH implementation changes the default cipher, MAC, and sometimes key-exchange algorithm lists, disabling unsafe legacy algorithms such as CBC ciphers and arcfour. An older SSH partner may support only those algorithms, leaving no mutually supported algorithm; typical errors are “No matching cipher found,” “No matching MAC algorithm found,” or “No matching kex algorithm found.”
For IBM i, the relevant PTFs upgraded OpenSSH from 6.6p1 to 6.9p1; the upgrade was made to address published CVE vulnerabilities and PCI compliance.

The preferred fix is to upgrade the remote SSH client or server so that it supports the safer default algorithms. As a temporary workaround, explicitly re-enable the required legacy algorithms in the appropriate IBM i configuration file: sshd_config when IBM i is the server, or ssh_config when IBM i is the client.
For V7R2 and later, the SSH configuration files are located under /QOpenSys/QIBM/UserData/SC1/OpenSSH/etc/.

ANSWER
HSM-enabled DataPower appliances support the export of private keys using the crypto-export command. For key export to work, various conditions must be met:

resolved_citations.text: On an HSM-enabled DataPower appliance, export a private key with the `crypto-export` command.

resolved_support.text: Second, the key to be exported must be exportable. The exportability of keys is immutable. It is determined at keygen time, and it is controlled by that command's exportable parameter. If a key was created outside of the appliance (not using keygen), then it is always considered exportable.

resolved_citations.text: The key must have been marked exportable when it was generated; key exportability is immutable. A key created outside the appliance is always considered exportable.

resolved_support.text:
* HSMs must be initialized and in the same key sharing domain on exporting and importing machines 
 * The private key in question must be marked exportable at keygen time (see keygen's exportable option) 
 * HSMs on exporting and importing machines must share internal key-wrapping keys (see hsm-clone-kwk command). A key-wrapping key is a key that encrypts another key.

First, the two HSMs in question must be both be initialized and in the same key sharing domain. This means that they must both be initialized in the same mode (both in Security Level 2 or both in Security Level 3). In Security Level 2 mode, they must have used the same hsm-domain parameter during hsm-reinit (this parameter has a default value that is the same on all appliances). In Security Level 3 mode, they must have used the same red PED key during hsm-reinit (and the second initialization must not have overwritten the key value from the first initialization).

Finally, before the crypto-export crypto-import sequence, the key-wrapping keys must be synchronized using the hsm-clone-kwk command. This command must be run four times: once on the source HSM appliance (with the key-wrapping key you are copying), once on the destination HSM appliance, once again on the source HSM appliance, and once again on the destination HSM appliance. Each time the command is run, it will need the output file from the previous step (as the input to the current step) which must be moved manually (usually with the copy command).
Once all of this has been done, then private keys may move from system to system with crypto-export and crypto-import.

resolved_citations.text: For moving a key between different HSM appliances, both HSMs must be initialized in the same key-sharing domain, and their key-wrapping keys must be synchronized with `hsm-clone-kwk` before using the `crypto-export`/`crypto-import` sequence.

resolved_support.text: Each HSM has a special key inside of it, the key-wrapping key, that is used to encrypt exported private keys (and to decrypt imported private keys). If the goal is to restore exported keys to the same appliance, then you don't need to worry about hsm-clone-kwk, red keys, or the hsm-domain parameter. That is because the key-wrapping key at import time will already match the key-wrapping key at export time (since the HSM device is the same). If the goal is to move exported keys from one appliance to another one, then all of the steps in this section must be followed :-

answer_parts.text: For the virtual appliance, download the virtual appliance upgrade package from IBM Fix Central. The listed package is “Virtual appliance upgrade,” dated 8 Dec 2014, with fix ID 2.5.0-WS-DPXC10-VIRT-FP0000004.

Before upgrading, read the version-specific DataPower upgrade documentation, save the current configuration, create a full system backup stored off the appliance, and verify that working administrative and backup privileged accounts are available.
Perform the upgrade by removing extraneous files, rebooting the appliance to release temporary storage, transferring the firmware image to the appliance, and installing the image.
If the upgrade from 5.0.0.8 to 6.0 or later fails, the supplied documentation does not identify the failure message or provide a 5.0-to-6.0 migration path specific to the virtual DataPower Appliance.

IBM later withdrew support for firmware levels 6.0 and 6.0.1 and advised customers on those or earlier levels to upgrade to the latest supported DataPower firmware releases; IBM recommended considering the latest 7.0 or 7.1 fix pack, or later, after testing configurations and surrounding applications.

Part 3: Preparing for the firmware upgrade. 
Review the installation instructions and prepare your appliance for the firmware upgrade. 
 1. Read the upgrade documentation in the version-specific DataPower information center. Instructions for accessing the correct information center is in the [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=2362&uid=swg21377654]IBM WebSphere DataPower Product Documentation Portal [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21377654] technical flash.

Part 3: Preparing for the firmware upgrade. 
Review the installation instructions and prepare your appliance for the firmware upgrade. 
 1. Read the upgrade documentation in the version-specific DataPower information center. Instructions for accessing the correct information center is in the [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=2362&uid=swg21377654]IBM WebSphere DataPower Product Documentation Portal [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21377654] technical flash. The steps in this flash provide additional information to use with the upgrade documentation in the information center. 
 2. Save the current configuration.  * From the WebGUI, click Save Config. 
     * From the command line, issue the write memory command.

3. Create a backup of the entire system, and store the configuration in a safe location off of the appliance. 
 4. Confirm that you have a working admin account and a back up privileged account that can change the password for the admin account, if needed. 
 5. Make sure that the passwords for both accounts were recently changed.

resolved_support.text:
ABSTRACT
 Effective 19 June 2016, IBM will withdraw support for the WebSphere DataPower SOA Appliances 6.0 and 6.0.1 firmware levels.

Customers running firmware level 6.0 or 6.0.1 (or any earlier level) are advised to plan to upgrade to the latest supported releases of WebSphere DataPower firmware in order to continue receiving technical support, as well as proactively avoiding problems that are already resolved. Refer to Supported Firmware versions and recommended upgrade levels [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21237631] for more information.

IBM recommends that users consider applying the 7.0 or 7.1 latest fixpack version (or later) of the firmware. Of course, in the case of upgrading firmware for any critical embedded system, IBM recommends that users test their configurations and surrounding applications before moving into production. To easily find the latest fixpack levels, please use this link: http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21237631 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21237631] .

answer_parts.text: The IBM security bulletin is available at http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21697107.

It covers multiple vulnerabilities in IBM SDK Java Technology Edition 7.1.4.10 and IBM Runtime Environment Java versions 7.0.10.10 and 7.1.4.10 used by IBM Integration Bus and WebSphere Message Broker; the issues were disclosed in the July 2017 IBM Java SDK updates.
CVE-2017-10115 could allow an unauthenticated attacker to obtain sensitive information; its CVSS base score is 7.5.
CVE-2017-10116 could allow an unauthenticated attacker to take control of the system; its CVSS base score is 8.3.
CVE-2017-10108 and CVE-2017-10109 could allow an unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial of service; each has a CVSS base score of 5.3.
The affected products include IBM Integration Bus V9.0.0.0–V9.0.0.8 and V10.0.0.0–V10.0.0.9, plus WebSphere Message Broker V7.0.0.0–V7.0.0.8 and V8.0.0.0–V8.0.0.9.
For remediation, APAR IT21764 is available in IBM Integration Bus fix packs 10.0.0.10 and 9.0.0.9; for WebSphere Message Broker V7 and V8, contact IBM Support to request the fix.
The bulletin states that no workarounds or mitigations are available.
For the complete list of IBM Java SDK vulnerabilities, consult the IBM Java SDK Security Bulletin in the References section: http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21986642.

answer_parts.text: The information is in IBM’s Security Bulletin for CVE-2014-8730 affecting IBM PureApplication System. The bulletin states that IBM PureApplication Server bundles IBM HTTP Server, which is vulnerable to a POODLE-like TLS padding attack that may allow a man-in-the-middle attacker to decrypt sensitive information from secure connections.

The bulletin covers IBM PureApplication System V1.1, V2.0, and V2.1; it explains that the vulnerability affects the IBM HTTP Server component bundled with WebSphere Application Server and the Web Application Pattern.

For remediation, apply the update to the Web Application pattern type included in IBM PureApplication System. The bulletin provides Fix Central links for V2.1 (webapp-2.0.4.1-sys and webapp-1.0.4.1-sys) and V2.0 (webapp-2.0.2.1-vaea-20150610).
The bulletin states that no workaround or mitigation is available and recommends verifying that applying the fix does not cause compatibility issues.

You can also consult IBM’s Secure Engineering Web Portal and IBM Product Security Incident Response Blog for related security information, and subscribe to IBM My Notifications for future security bulletins.

answer_parts.text: The security bulletin information is provided in IBM’s bulletin for IBM PureApplication System. It covers a TLS padding vulnerability exploited through a POODLE-like attack.

The vulnerability is CVE-2014-8730. IBM PureApplication Server bundles IBM HTTP Server, whose failure to check TLS CBC padding bytes could allow a man-in-the-middle attacker to decrypt sensitive information and calculate plaintext from secure connections. The CVSS base score is 4.3.
Affected releases listed are IBM PureApplication System V1.1, V2.0, and V2.1.

For remediation, apply an update to the Web Application pattern type included with IBM PureApplication System. Fix Central links are provided for V2.1 and V2.0; the bulletin separately lists V1.1 and earlier.
The bulletin lists no workaround or mitigation and advises verifying that applying the fix does not cause compatibility issues.

You can find related IBM security information through the IBM Secure Engineering Web Portal and the IBM Product Security Incident Response Blog. IBM also recommends subscribing to My Notifications for future security bulletins.

resolved_support.text: SECURITY BULLETIN

SUMMARY
 Transport Layer Security (TLS) padding vulnerability via a POODLE (Padding Oracle On Downgraded Legacy Encryption) like attack affects IBM PureApplication System.

resolved_citations.text: The security bulletin information is provided in IBM’s bulletin for IBM PureApplication System. It covers a TLS padding vulnerability exploited through a POODLE-like attack.

resolved_support.text:
VULNERABILITY DETAILS
CVEID: CVE-2014-8730 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2014-8730]
DESCRIPTION: IBM PureApplication Server bundles IBM HTTP Server, which could allow a remote attacker to obtain sensitive information, caused by the failure to check the contents of the padding bytes when using CBC cipher suites of some TLS implementations. A remote user with the ability to conduct a man-in-the-middle attack could exploit this vulnerability via a POODLE (Padding Oracle On Downgraded Legacy Encryption) like attack to decrypt sensitive information and calculate the plain text of secure connections.
CVSS Base Score: 4.3
CVSS Temporal Score: See https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/99216 [https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/99216] for the current score
CVSS Environmental Score*: Undefined
CVSS Vector: (AV:N/AC:M/Au:N/C:P/I:N/A:N)

answer_parts.text: A stale connection occurs when the underlying network connection to the database is no longer valid, while WebSphere Application Server still considers the pooled data-source connection active. A firewall or remote database may discard connections that remain idle, causing the subsequent database access to fail with StaleConnectionException.

The problem commonly appears after a period of database inactivity—for example, when the first user accesses an RTS/Decision Center server after it was idle overnight, or when a Portal server attempts to access its database after inactivity.

For WebSphere Application Server, set the data-source connection pool Minimum connections to 0. This prevents connections from being retained solely to satisfy a minimum-pool requirement and causes WAS to remove connections after inactivity.
Configure Unused timeout and Reap timeout so their sum does not exceed any network-level idle connection timeout.
In the WAS administrative console, navigate to Resources → JDBC → Data sources, edit the Connection pools settings for each applicable data source, and restart the servers after making the changes.

resolved_support.text:
CAUSE
The underlying network connection for a data source is no longer valid although the data source itself remains considered active from the WebSphere Application Server data source connection pool management perspective. An attempt by a JRules module to try and access its data base through one such data source connection provided by the Application Server may then fail. 
The network connection of a data source may become invalid for a number of reasons, one typical example is that a firewall between the Application Server and the Database has a policy to discard network connections that remain idle for some time.

CAUSE
The Portal connection to the database is closed externally by a firewall or by the remote database due to inactivity. Because Portal is still holding onto this connection, we still think the connection is available, and so receive the stale connection exception.

resolved_citations.text: A stale connection occurs when the underlying network connection to the database is no longer valid, while WebSphere Application Server still considers the pooled data-source connection active. A firewall or remote database may discard connections that remain idle, causing the subsequent database access to fail with StaleConnectionException.

resolved_support.text:
SYMPTOM
The problem may occur when a JRules or ODM module accesses its data source after a period of database access inactivity. For example:

* The first user accessing a RTS / DC server that remained idle overnight experiences a failure upon logging and the server log shows an com.ibm.websphere.ce.cm.StaleConnectionException occurred at that time. 
 * After a RES server has been processing execution requests normally for some time, an attempt to deploy a ruleset update fails and the server log shows an com.ibm.websphere.ce.cm.StaleConnectionException occurred upon an attempt to invalidate a ruleset or to retrieve its definition.

PROBLEM
Stale connections can occur after Portal server has been idle for a period of time and attempts to access the database.

SYMPTOM
After a period of inactivity, the Portal server becomes unresponsive.

resolved_citations.text: The problem commonly appears after a period of database inactivity—for example, when the first user accesses an RTS/Decision Center server after it was idle overnight, or when a Portal server attempts to access its database after inactivity.

resolved_support.text:
RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Configure the WebSphere Application Server data source connection pool [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/wasinfo/v7r0/index.jsp?topic=/com.ibm.websphere.nd.multiplatform.doc/info/ae/ae/udat_conpoolset.html] so as to eliminate occurrences of StaleConnectionException :

* Set the Minimum connections to 0 to avoid situations where a connection is kept in the pool to meet the minimum requirement, even though it may have been idle for longer than Unused timeout 
 * Set the values for Unused timeout and Reap timeout so that the sum does not exceed any network level idle connection timeout

RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
The solution is to reduce the Minimum Connections to 0 on the data source.
This will cause WAS to remove all connections after a period of inactivity.

answer_parts.text: The error indicates that the Installation Manager repository is missing required ZIP artifacts. This can occur when IBM Packaging Utility deletes additional files while deleting a package or fix from a repository.

Use IBM Packaging Utility to recopy the affected BPM fix or package from the original source into the repository that is missing the files. The issue is fixed in Packaging Utility version 1.6, so use that version or later.

Alternatively, obtain a complete IBM Installation Manager repository image and extract all repository parts into the same directory before retrying the installation. IBM documents that the PART1 and PART2 images must be extracted under the same directory.

For the SCA component, IBM provides ZIP files for creating a local repository and states that IBM Installation Manager must point to the SCA local import repository when using a local repository for future maintenance.

After repairing or replacing the repository, restart IBM Installation Manager and retry the fix-pack installation. If the problem remains, check the repository for consistency and review Installation History to identify the package with the issue; IBM also advises contacting IBM customer support.

Its related-information links include the IBM Secure Engineering Web Portal at http://www.ibm.com/security/secure-engineering/bulletins.html and the IBM Product Security Incident Response Blog at http://www.ibm.com/blogs/psirt.
For the affected IBM OS Images, the bulletin covers IBM OS Image for Red Hat Linux Systems 2.0.0.1 and earlier and IBM OS Image for AIX 2.0.0.1 and earlier.
The bulletin describes CVE-2015-0410 as a Security-component vulnerability that could allow a remote attacker to cause denial of service, with a CVSS base score of 5.
It describes CVE-2014-6593 as a JSSE-component vulnerability with partial confidentiality and integrity impact and no availability impact, with a CVSS base score of 4.

For deployed Red Hat Linux-based and AIX virtual machines on IBM PureApplication Systems, IBM directs users to apply the IBM PureApplication System fix; the listed fixes are Java Update for Linux and Java Update for AIX.

The bulletin states that users should import the fix into the Emergency Fix catalogue, apply it to deployed virtual machines, and restart the deployed instance afterward. The update upgrades IBM Java JDK 7.0 to SR8 FP10 interim fix and IBM Java JDK 6.0 to SR16 FP3 interim fix.
IBM lists no workaround or mitigation and recommends subscribing to My Notifications for future security bulletins.

answer_parts.text: The symptoms are consistent with a corrupted PolicyList file. In the documented case, missing entries or properties in `$NCHOME/impact/etc/policylist` caused cluster replication problems; the last item attempted before replication stalled was the PolicyList.

Rebuild the PolicyList file. Perform the procedure as the user who installed and runs Impact: stop WebSphere using `$NCHOME/bin/ewas.sh stop -user wasadmin -password netcool`, back up the existing `NCI1_policylist` as `NCI1_policylist.orig`, rebuild or recreate `NCI1_policylist` with the Impact SVN utilities (`nci_startsvn` and `nci_addsvn`), and then restart WebSphere with `$NCHOME/bin/ewas.sh start`.

The supplied documentation also describes a separate expected cluster behavior: policy activators run only on the primary, while the event processor is normally active on the secondary. Events processed through a policy activator therefore run only on the server where that activator is running; Impact itself has no configuration to change this behavior.

resolved_support.text:
ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  Unlike events read by event readers, events processed by a
   policy launched by a policy activator are not processed by the
   event processor.  The implication of that is that in a
   normally-functioning cluster, events processed via an activated
   policy will only ever be processed on the current primary
   server.

PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED:                                              *
   * All Impact Users                                             *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION:                                         *
   * Question re policy activator: Q: Why doesn't the policy      *
   * activator run on the secondary cluster                       *
   * member? Can I do anything about it?                          *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION:                                              *
   * It's expected behaviour that policy activators run only on   *
   * the primary.                                                 *
   *                                                              *
   * The only service normally active on a secondary server in    *
   * the cluster is the event processor.  The event processor     *
   * does not handle                                              *
   * events from policies activated by a policy activator, only   *
   * events read from event reader queues.  Therefore an event    *
   * processed via a policy activator will only ever be processed *
   * on the Impact server where the policy activator service is   *
   * running.                                                     *
   *                                                              *
   * There is no way of configuring this to behave differently in *
   * Impact itself currently.  However, it is possible to         *
   * activate a policy to run on the secondary by using a cron    *
   * job to run nci_trigger at intervals.  But the risk with this *
   * approach is that it will have no failover                    *
   * capability.  Another idea is to put the policies inside an   *
   * event reader of their own and set that event reader to have  *
   * a very                                                       *
   * long polling interval - the same frequency as your policy    *
   * activator.                                                   *
   ****************************************************************

 After logging into FileNet Workplace XT, a java.lang.NullPointerException error is logged when bootstrapping the object store or when accessing Site Preferences/Access Role.
at com.filenet.wcm.apps.server.ui.info.prefs.PrefAccessRolesInfoPage.renderRoleMembers(PrefAccessRolesInfoPage.java:254)

at com.filenet.wcm.apps.server.ui.info.prefs.PrefBootstrapInfoPage.render(PrefBootstrapInfoPage.java:303)

CAUSE
This behavior may occur if an invalid entry has been specified in the User Display Name Attribute or Group Display Name Attribute setting in the Directory Services Configuration in FileNet Enterprise Manager (FEM).

Workplace XT attempts to resolve the user names and groups defined within the Access Roles based on the Directory Service configuration defined in FEM. If the user name query resolves to null or if there is an invalid entry a NullPointerException error may occur.

resolved_support.text:
RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
If there are CSV document already in the content repository with a mime type that is not text/csv, then in order to view them in a text editor (ex. Notepad), you may use the following workaround:
- save the document to the local machine with .dat extension
- right click on the .dat file and click Open With... 
- click 'Choose your default program...'
- then select Notepad or another text editor of your choice
- select the checkbox 'Always use the selected program to open this type of file'
The other alternative is to change the mimetype of the document in the content repository using a custom solution written using the repository's client APIs.

answer_parts.text: Look first for a hostname change and semaphore-ID clashes with other software. On distributed platforms including iSeries, MQ can lose fault tolerance for semaphore-ID clashes after the system hostname changes.

Check `/var/mqm/sockets/@SYSTEM/qmgrlocl` for a directory named after the local hostname. Before the fix, MQ checked or created this directory only during installation, not during `strmqm`; the corrected code checks and creates it during `strmqm` if necessary.

resolved_support.text:
Platforms affected:
   All Distributed (iSeries, all Unix and Windows)
   ****************************************************************
   PROBLEM SUMMARY:
   The path /var/mqm/sockets/@SYSTEM/qmgrlocl should contain a
   directory named after the hostname of the local machine.

The said directory was checked and created only at the time
   WebSphere MQ was installed on the machine. But during strmqm,
   there was no check that the directory existed.

If the system hostname does not change, there is no problem at
   all. But if the system hostname is changed, WebSphere MQ code
   will not check the path containing the new hostname directory
   or attempt to create it.

PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  The WebSphere MQ code has been changed. During strmqm, there
   is now a check for the existence of the directory named above.
   If the directory does not exist, an attempt will be made to
   create it.

resolved_citations.text: Check `/var/mqm/sockets/@SYSTEM/qmgrlocl` for a directory named after the local hostname. Before the fix, MQ checked or created this directory only during installation, not during `strmqm`; the corrected code checks and creates it during `strmqm` if necessary.

resolved_support.text:
After a hostname change, WebSphere MQ code will use another
   scheme for allocating semaphore IDs, but if there is a clash
   with a semaphore ID in use by other software on the machine,
   then WebSphere MQ trace functionality can become disabled.

The semaphore IDs in question are only those used in relation
   to WebSphere MQ trace. It is only the functionality of MQ
   trace that is potentially affected by this issue.

resolved_citations.text: The documented semaphore clash affects semaphore IDs used for WebSphere MQ trace; the stated direct impact is that MQ trace functionality can become disabled.
